driver_layer.verification: rg -n '\bunsafe\b' drivers/block/rnull returned no matches after hardening and runtime fixes

unsafe_sites.kind: intrusive configfs callback and container_of boundary
unsafe_sites.invariant: Subsystem, group, and item storage remain pinned and release/drop_item callbacks reconstruct the owning Rust object exactly once.
unsafe_sites.why_unsafe_exists: configfs hands raw C pointers back into Rust and requires container_of reconstruction plus raw page buffer access.

unsafe_sites.invariant: HrTimer owner stays pinned for the entire callback lifetime and callback reconstruction from the raw timer pointer always points back to the same owner.
unsafe_sites.why_unsafe_exists: hrtimer callbacks arrive as raw C pointers and require container_of plus raw timer control functions.

unsafe_sites.invariant: Each blk-mq request private area is initialized once, refcounted through completion, timeout, and poll paths, and dropped exactly once when blk-mq exits the request.
unsafe_sites.why_unsafe_exists: The block layer owns request storage and only exposes raw request pointers and PDU accessors.

unsafe_sites.invariant: driver_data always points at valid queue-mapping state for the lifetime of the tag set and blk_mq_free_tag_set is paired exactly once with successful allocation.
unsafe_sites.why_unsafe_exists: blk-mq registration, queue mapping, and driver_data handoff are C-owned raw pointer flows.
notes: TagSet carries unsafe impl Send and Sync to support controller-level shared tag pools.
memory-debug matrix-core runtime covered shared_tags queue-count updates without new dmesg anomalies on the Rust candidate.

unsafe_sites.kind: gendisk allocation and queue_data foreign ownership
unsafe_sites.invariant: queue_data foreign storage is transferred to the block layer at build time and reclaimed exactly once when the gendisk is dropped.
unsafe_sites.why_unsafe_exists: blk_mq_alloc_disk, set_capacity, disk_name writes, and queuedata extraction are all raw C operations.

unsafe_sites.kind: opaque C struct init/exit and concurrent checks
unsafe_sites.invariant: badblocks_init and badblocks_exit are paired, disabled state never triggers the helper WARN_ON path, and the wrapper only exposes thread-safe operations after initialization.
unsafe_sites.why_unsafe_exists: struct badblocks is C-owned state with initialization and show/check/set helpers exposed through bindings.

unsafe_sites.invariant: Helpers remain generic bindings bridges only and do not encode rnull-owned driver state or lifetimes.
unsafe_sites.why_unsafe_exists: blk-mq inline helpers, request-iteration macros, and hrtimer inline wrappers are not directly expressible from Rust on this baseline tree.

open_items.reason: Hardening reduced the helper surface but did not yet prove the remaining generic helpers can be retired on this tree.
The frozen mbps target still lacks credible C-baseline runtime closure under the current harness.
